To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the binding of proteins to different membranes is dependent on several factors, including the protein and the buffer used for electroblotting or for immunoassays.
the performance of membranes in immuno-assays and electroblots depends on the nature of the membrane and the buffer used.

the membranes' ability (a) to bind increasing amounts protein, (b) to bind proteins from different sources, (c) to retain proteins during incubation times, (d) to bind different proteins in different buffers and (e) to bind proteins during the electrotransfer of different proteins to the membranes, were found to differ greatly for the membranes investigated.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the study of the physical and chemical properties of nitrocelluloses, nylons and polyvinylidenefluorides (PVDF) membranes which are commonly used to bind and immobilize proteins in blotting, dot binding and immunoassay techniques.
the use of membranes as adsorbents of proteins in dot blot assays and in electroblotting of proteins to membranes for immunological analysis.
the development of new materials, methods, devices and systems for the separation and analysis of biological materials.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the performance of membranes as protein adsorbents is dependent upon the specific application.
there is no one membrane which is best in all situations, but rather that the choice of a suitable membrane depends on the application and the buffer system used.
no one membrane is superior to all other types for all applications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there is a need for more information to be provided with each membrane to enable the user to make an informed choice of membrane for each particular application.
the use of PVDF and nylon as protein adsorbents in immunoassay systems is limited to the use of low concentrations of protein and the use of low ionic strength buffers.
PVDF and Nylon are better than nitrocelluloses as protein adsorbents for use in immunoassay, and PVDF is superior to the other two membranes when used for electroblotting.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the choice of membrane is a critical factor in the success of a blotting assay, and that a range of factors should be considered when selecting a membrane for a particular assay.
there is no single best membrane for all applications.
the selection of the most appropriate membrane for a specific assay is a complex process which should be based on a number of different criteria.
